quizName: DMV Practice Test #2 25 Questions • Passing Score 20

questions.question: You can increase your visibility by:

options.text: Adding extra lights to your motorcycle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Adding extra lights to your motorcycle.
questions.explanation: You can increase visibility by wearing bright or reflective clothing. You can also add extra lights to your motorcycle, use your turn signals, and flash your brake light when needed. These actions help other drivers notice you.

questions.question: When carrying a passenger on a motorcycle, you must:

options.text: Have a seat large enough for two riders.
Have only one set of footrests.
Not require the passenger to wear protective clothing.
Add a sticker to the brake light to warn other drivers.

questions.correctAnswerText: Have a seat large enough for two riders.
questions.explanation: Your motorcycle must have a seat large enough for two riders. It must have footrests for the passenger. Your passenger should wear the same protective gear you wear.

questions.question: A rectangular sign may be a:
questions.explanation: Regulatory signs like speed limit signs are usually rectangular. They are white with black letters or symbols. You must follow the rules posted on these signs.

questions.question: Goggles will:

options.text: Be equally as effective as a face shield.
Offer the same protection as a windshield.
Provide protection for your entire face.

questions.explanation: Goggles protect only your eyes, not your whole face. A face shield is recommended because it protects your entire face. A windshield alone is not enough protection.

questions.question: When carrying a passenger, you should:

options.text: Prepare and adjust your motorcycle for the passenger.
Ride the same way as you would without a passenger.
Have footrests for only you, the operator.
Teach the passenger after you start riding.

questions.correctAnswerText: Prepare and adjust your motorcycle for the passenger.
questions.explanation: Your motorcycle must be properly equipped and adjusted for a passenger. It needs separate footrests for the passenger and a seat wide enough for two people. You may need to adjust your headlight, tire pressure, and suspension for the extra weight.

questions.question: Your primary source for information about your motorcycle should be:
questions.explanation: Your owner's manual is the best source for information about your specific motorcycle. It contains details about how to operate it, its specifications, and recommended maintenance.

questions.question: If you wait one hour to ride after having one alcoholic drink:

options.text: You cannot be arrested for drinking and driving.
Your riding skills will not be affected by the alcohol.
Effects from the alcohol may still remain.
You will be fine as long as you ride slowly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Effects from the alcohol may still remain.
questions.explanation: Your body can eliminate about one drink per hour. However, alcohol can build up in your system. Even if you drink slowly, alcohol can still affect your ability to ride safely.

questions.question: Shifting into a lower gear causes an effect similar to:
questions.explanation: Shifting into a lower gear slows your motorcycle, similar to using the brakes. This is called engine braking.

questions.question: To prevent injury when riding on a slippery surface, a motorcyclist should:
questions.explanation: On a slippery surface, slow down. Sudden movements can cause your motorcycle to skid. Do not ride on the shoulder to avoid a slippery road.

questions.question: Signals on a motorcycle:

options.text: Are even more important than signals on cars and trucks.
Should not be used unless another vehicle is right next to you.
Are less important than signals on cars and trucks.

questions.correctAnswerText: Are even more important than signals on cars and trucks.
questions.explanation: Motorcyclists are more vulnerable than car and truck drivers. Using signals correctly is even more important for your safety.

questions.question: Which of these is NOT a good choice for riding clothes?

options.text: A jacket and pants that fully cover your arms and legs
Boots or shoes that cover your ankles
A baseball cap to cover your hair

questions.correctAnswerText: A baseball cap to cover your hair
questions.explanation: To protect yourself from injury, wear a DOT-approved helmet, face or eye protection, a sturdy jacket and long pants, boots or shoes that cover and support your ankles, and durable gloves.

questions.question: When riding on a bridge grating, you should:

options.text: Always ride on the far right side of the lane.
Always ride on the far left side of the lane.
Stay relaxed, keep steady speed, and ride straight across.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stay relaxed, keep steady speed, and ride straight across.
questions.explanation: Bridge gratings may cause your motorcycle to weave slightly. This is usually safe, so stay calm and cross at a steady speed. Zigzagging to fight the weave is dangerous because you lose lane control.

questions.question: How often should you do a pre-ride inspection?
questions.explanation: Check your motorcycle before every ride to prevent mechanical problems. Small issues on a motorcycle are more dangerous than on a car.

questions.question: How can you reduce your risk of a crash?

options.text: Keep your intentions hidden from other drivers
Always stay within one foot of another vehicle

questions.explanation: Stay visible by using your signals, brake light, and good lane position. Keep space around your motorcycle and watch the road ahead, behind, and beside you.

questions.question: A three-wheeled motorcycle:

options.text: Handles curves the same as a two-wheeled motorcycle
Handles curves differently than a two-wheeled motorcycle
Should not be used in curves
Should use the shoulder when turning

questions.correctAnswerText: Handles curves differently than a two-wheeled motorcycle
questions.explanation: Three-wheeled motorcycles and motorcycles with sidecars turn differently than two-wheeled motorcycles.

questions.question: Which sign is yellow with black letters or symbols?
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black letters or symbols. They alert drivers to upcoming road conditions.

questions.question: A plastic face shield protects you from:
questions.explanation: A face shield protects you from wind, dust, dirt, rain, insects, and pebbles thrown up by other vehicles, plus injury in a crash.

questions.question: When should you wear a jacket while riding?

options.text: Only on rides longer than half an hour

questions.explanation: Always wear a long-sleeved jacket when riding, even in warm weather. It protects you from the sun and helps prevent dehydration.

questions.question: What is the main active ingredient in marijuana?
questions.explanation: The main active substance in marijuana is tetrahydrocannabinol, or THC.

questions.question: How can you be seen better at an intersection?

options.text: Swerve in your lane to get attention

questions.explanation: Use your headlight and position your motorcycle so oncoming drivers can see you clearly. Keep space around your motorcycle so you can react quickly if needed.

questions.question: When you borrow a motorcycle, what should you do?

options.text: You don't need to check the tire pressure.
It will handle exactly like your own bike.
The owner will check the brakes, so you don't have to.
Leave extra space between you and other vehicles to give yourself time to react.

questions.correctAnswerText: Leave extra space between you and other vehicles to give yourself time to react.
questions.explanation: Always do the same safety checks on a borrowed motorcycle as you would on your own. Ride carefully on an unfamiliar bike and keep extra space when stopping.

questions.question: What should you do if a driver is tailgating you?

options.text: Move to the side so they can share your lane.

questions.explanation: The safest way to handle a tailgater is to let them get ahead of you. If it's safe, change lanes and let them pass. Speeding up may make it worse by encouraging them to tailgate at a higher speed.

questions.question: When stopped behind another vehicle, what should you do?

options.text: Get as close as possible to the vehicle.
Keep space between your motorcycle and the vehicle ahead.
Don't use your rearview mirrors to watch traffic behind you.
Look for ways to squeeze through stopped traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep space between your motorcycle and the vehicle ahead.
questions.explanation: Stay well behind the vehicle in front of you, even when stopped. This gives you room to escape if the vehicle backs up or another vehicle comes too fast from behind.

questions.question: Before riding, what should you NOT check on your tires?
questions.explanation: Before each ride, check the air pressure, tread, and general wear of your tires. Shininess is not important for safety.

questions.question: What should you inspect before riding?

options.text: How much padding your seat has

questions.explanation: Before every ride, do a full check of your motorcycle. Check the tires, oil and fluids, headlight, tail light, turn signals, brake light, clutch and throttle, mirrors, brakes, and horn.
